claims.claim: Earth is a dynamic structure whose surface changes in different ways and at different time scales.
Plate movement can build mountains, and sticking then slipping along moving plates can release energy as earthquakes.
Weathering and erosion shape landforms over long periods through water, wind, ice, and gravity.
Weathering loosens or alters material in place, whereas erosion moves it; deposition is accumulation of transported sediment.
Earth systems interact: weathering and erosion connect the geosphere with water, air, life, and gravity, while tectonic processes shape landscapes.
A landscape can record multiple processes, so an explanation should identify observations, propose a process, and state the scale or uncertainty rather than assume one visible feature has one cause.
